exercise1.prompt: Slices look like list slices and behave differently in one important way.

hiddenCases.name: three items leave one in the middle

exercise1.hint: A slice from 1 to -1 drops one from each end, and slices clamp rather than raise when there is nothing left to take.

choices: A view onto the same data
questions.explain: Writing into the slice writes into the original. It is the single biggest behavioural difference from list slicing, and it is a feature: no copy is made.

questions.prompt: How do you take a slice you can safely modify?
questions.explain: copy() makes a new array; building a list first also detaches from the buffer. Either gives you something of your own.
Negative indexes count from the end, exactly as in lists.
